sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered why some string operations in Java are slow? Let's fix that!

• Why regular strings can be inefficient
• How StringBuilder and StringBuffer make string operations faster
• When to use each one (they're not the same!)

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine you're building a LEGO tower. With regular strings, every time you add a block, you have to:
1. Take a photo of your current tower
2. Build a new tower with the extra block
3. Throw away the old tower

That's how regular String concatenation works - it creates new objects every time!

StringBuilder and StringBuffer are like having a reusable LEGO board where you can just keep adding blocks without starting over.

• **StringBuilder**: Your personal LEGO board (not thread-safe, but fast)
• **StringBuffer**: A shared LEGO board with safety locks (thread-safe, slightly slower)
• Both let you modify strings without creating new objects each time

sections.title: ⚡ Key Points
points: ✓ StringBuilder is faster than String for multiple modifications
✓ StringBuffer is thread-safe (use in multi-threaded apps)
✓ Both use the same methods (append(), insert(), delete(), etc.)
✓ Always convert back to String when you're done modifying
✓ Use StringBuilder for single-threaded apps (better performance)

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
dos: Use StringBuilder for loops with string concatenation
Initialize with enough capacity if you know the final size
Use toString() when you need the final result
donts: Don't use String concatenation (+) in loops
Don't forget toString() when you need a String
Don't use StringBuffer unless you need thread safety
sections.protip: For simple concatenations (like 2-3 strings), regular String is fine. Use StringBuilder when you're doing 5+ modifications or working in loops.

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where you'll see these in action:

examples.how: Building large log messages by appending multiple lines efficiently
Constructing complex JSON/XML strings without performance penalties
Dynamically creating SQL queries by appending conditions

problem.description: Write a method that takes an array of strings and joins them with commas, but with a twist: the last two elements should be joined with "and" instead of a comma. Use StringBuilder for efficiency.
hints: Loop through all elements except the last two
Handle the last two elements specially
Don't forget the edge case of empty array!
problem.explanation: We use StringBuilder to efficiently build the result. The loop handles all elements except the last two, then we add the special "and" conjunction before the final element. This approach is much more efficient than using regular string concatenation.

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Use append(), insert(), delete() for modifications
📌 Convert to String with toString() when done
📌 Ready to optimize your string operations!
